about: Amr's context sheets S11-S114: the weather where the visitor is, the time of day, Egyptian, Islamic, Coptic and international days, the seasons, the toolkit's own moments, play, and one sheet each for 50 of the website's tools (S65-S114, the tools-* groups). One source for the ChatGPT prompts (scripts/build-mascot-context-brief.mjs), the pack builder (scripts/build-mascot-packs.py) and the scene tests. Slot 1 of every sheet is the standard stance; `slots` are slots 2-8. A slot's `kind` is how the builder lines it up (feet unless it says hip).
addendum:
CONTEXT SHEETS (S11 and later). These sheets give Amr a prop or a moment from the weather, the time of day, a holiday, a season or his work.
- The sheet text describes each prop once. Draw that same prop, the same size and colours, in every slot that uses it. Props are simple, solid, slightly toy-like objects with clean shapes and bold colours, big enough to read when he is 100 pixels tall. A prop stays inside his slot and never hides his face unless a slot says so.
- His clothes never change: no coats, jackets, costumes or hats unless a slot asks for one, and then it goes over his usual clothes. Wherever his hair shows, it is exactly the haircut in ref-hair.
- Draw no weather and no effects: no rain, raindrops, puddles, snow, snowflakes, wind lines, sun rays, steam, smoke, sparks, sparkles, confetti, fireworks, light beams or musical notes. The website adds those. Act the weather and the moment with his body and face.
- No writing, letters or numbers on any prop. No other people and no animals; a toy only where a slot asks for one.
- Food and drink are always held in his hand, never floating, unless a slot says it was just tossed.

rounds.title: Every day: the weather and the hour
rounds.note: These play on any day, so they make the biggest difference first.

rounds.title: Coming up, in date order
rounds.note: From November 2026: winter, Christmas and New Year, Isra and Mi'raj (5 January 2027), 25 January, Valentine's Day, Ramadan (from about 8 February), Eid al-Fitr (about 9 March), Mother's Day, Pi Day and April Fools, Earth Day, Coptic Easter and Sham el-Nessim (2 and 3 May), Labour Day, Eid al-Adha (about 16 May), summer, the Mawlid (about 14 August), Nayrouz, back to school and Halloween.

rounds.title: The toolkit and play
rounds.note: Any time: cards, votes, timers, kudos, releases, and what he does when the visitor is idle.

rounds.title: Tools, batch A: planning, and impediments
rounds.note: Opened most often: sprint capacity and goals, refinement, forecasts, roadmaps, cross-team syncs and blockers.

rounds.title: Tools, batch B: review, retro and delivery
rounds.note: Sprint review, retro actions, premortem, six hats, canvas, and the delivery charts.

rounds.title: Tools, batch C: team and people
rounds.note: Feature flags, health checks, safety, mood, agreements, Definition of Done, skills, roles, one-on-ones and stakeholders.

rounds.title: Tools, batch D: prioritize and decide
rounds.note: Change, ranking, WSJF, MoSCoW, cost of delay, value and effort, Kano, buy-a-feature, Eisenhower and decisions.

rounds.title: Tools, batch E: outcomes and quality
rounds.note: Cynefin, OKRs, NPS, hypotheses, interviews, the opportunity tree, assumptions, risks, tech debt and flaky tests.

tools_addendum:
TOOL SHEETS (S65 and later). Each sheet gives Amr the props of one tool on the website.
- REFERENCES IN THIS ROUND: ref-1 is his standard stance. ref-current shows him as he is today: his face, his haircut from the front, turned and looking down, and the smooth way he is rendered; use it wherever the master block says ref-hair or ref-2. ref-hair-fix-3 shows the haircut to match (TARGET) and the hair to avoid (NOT THIS). ref-3 shows poses he already has. ref-4 is the approved S01 sheet: match its face and haircut exactly.
- HAIR (this overrides any other hair description): exactly the haircut in ref-4 and in the TARGET row of ref-hair-fix-3. Short all over and close to the shape of his skull, with no dome, helmet or volume on top; a little more length at the front, brushed slightly up and back; a thin, even layer of hair down each side to the top of his ears, which show just past it. Very dark brown-black with soft highlights on top: never flat black and never brown. A fine, smooth texture with no curls, coils, waves or bumpy outline. The same haircut in all 8 slots.
- RENDERING: smooth, soft, even shading on his face, skin and shirt, exactly like ref-4 and ref-current. No angular, faceted, patchy or painterly shading, and no extra wrinkles.
- PROPS: only the props the sheet names, each drawn the same in every slot that uses it: simple, solid, slightly toy-like, with clean shapes and bold colours, big enough to read when he is 100 pixels tall. Charts, boards and screens show plain shapes and colours only: no text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere, unless the sheet allows a single symbol. Props never hide his face.
